title: The Last Choir Revisited
premise: Sebastian Sterling has spent nine years hiding among the ledgers of the Guild of Improbable Things, trading in bottled memories and secondhand miracles while keeping his own name off every page. When the old gods stir beneath the mountain and begin answering prayers with ruinous bargains, Sebastian learns his hedge-witch mistress sold his soul to the Undercourt decades ago to buy his apprenticeship—and the dragon whose dying fire seals the Court's power is the last thing keeping his debt from being called in. As the guild fractures between those who worship the returning gods and those who remember what they devour, Sebastian gathers a found family of ledger-clerks, a disgraced god-touched singer, and the dragon's last keeper to steal his soul back before the final flame gutters out. In the end, he burns his own page from the Court's ledger at the cost of the guild itself, discovering that a name freely given is the only inheritance that cannot be stolen.
about_author: Ada Winterbourne is the pen name of a former cathedral archivist who spent a decade cataloguing hymnals no one sang anymore. She writes fantasy about the small, stubborn people who keep the world's paperwork—and occasionally steal it back.

chapters.title: Entries in Invisible Ink
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He catalogs a shipment of bottled last words for the Guild of Improbable Things, revealing his meticulous invisibility and quiet longing for the hedge-witch who abandoned him. When a prayer slips through the guild's wards and is actually answered, the ledgers rewrite themselves overnight. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine, the first crack in his safe small life.

chapters.title: The Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A guild client's wish for her drowned son comes true—at the cost of every firstborn in her village. Sebastian traces the transaction to the Undercourt beneath the mountain and finds his own childhood signature in an old debt ledger, sold by his mistress. Emotional beat: betrayal and vertigo as his hidden past surfaces in ink he recognizes.

chapters.title: What the Dragon Remembers
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, the dragon's last keeper. She tends the dying ember of Vaskalorth, whose fire seals the Undercourt's power, and watches the god-touched pilgrims gathering on the mountain. She recognizes Sebastian's guild seal when he arrives seeking answers. Emotional beat: grief for a fading companion and wary hope at an unexpected ally.

chapters.title: A Choir of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Back at the guild, the masters split—some kneel to the returning gods, offering the guild's trade routes as temples. Sebastian allies with Odile, a disgraced singer whose voice once carried god-prayers and who lost it as payment. Emotional beat: found family forming in the margins, defiance kindling in a man built to hide.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She teaches Sebastian the old god-songs that can open the Undercourt's doors, revealing her own debt: her voice was collateral for her sister's life, and her sister now serves the Court willingly. Sebastian realizes the Court collects inheritance—debt passed blood to blood. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared damage, and the horror of legacies as chains.

chapters.title: The Descent Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The trio infiltrates the guild's deepest vault for the original contract and finds his mistress's confession: she sold his soul to buy him nine years of safety from the gods who wanted him as their vessel. The masters discover the theft. Emotional beat: fury and tenderness entwined—betrayal reframed as a terrible, loving bargain.

chapters.title: Where the Fire Gutters
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Vaskalorth's flame fails as the Court's power floods the mountain; the god-worshipping masters seize the guild and offer Sebastian to the Court as payment. Maren carries the last ember down into the dark, knowing it will cost the dragon what remains of his life. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, loyalty outweighing survival.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In the Undercourt, the old gods offer him everything he secretly wanted—belonging, power, a name sung by choirs—in exchange for becoming their vessel. His mistress's soul, still held as collateral, begs him to accept. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive, corruption dressed as homecoming.

chapters.title: Burn the Page
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, climax. With Odile's recovered voice and Maren's ember, Sebastian sings the unbinding hymn and feeds his contract to the dragon-fire, erasing his debt—and with it, the guild's charter, the Court's anchor, and the gods' hold on the world. Vaskalorth's last flame goes out with the gods' power. Emotional beat: triumphant self-erasure that becomes self-definition.

chapters.title: A Name Freely Given
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, resolution. The guild lies in ruins, but its clerks, Odile, and Maren rebuild it as something new: a house that keeps names instead of debts. Sebastian writes his own name into the first ledger, freely given, and lights a candle for his mistress. Emotional beat: quiet peace—inheritance reclaimed as choice, family as the ledger he keeps himself.
